title: Caleb Williams on making corrections during the bye week | Press Conference
text: How much of the break was for you to recover physically?  I know you're not on the injured list.  You had surgery on your Achilles tendon, but just to have a week off and do nothing physically... Yes, that was good.  It's always good to have some time off, especially since the injury.  I was always on the go , whether it was for rehab, movies, or of course, games.  The weeks were short, the weeks long, everything was possible.  So the schedules changed, and so on.   So it was good to have a break and reorient myself mentally and physically . Then I either did nothing at all or just had a little more or less time to relax and maybe not move around so much How does the Achilles tendon feel? Good. Looks good, but yes, I've noticed that you haven't been running much in the last two weeks I said that I didn't have to How does it feel? Feels good.  Feels good.  Yes You said it would affect you for the whole season.  You thought so. Not to impair it, but rather to make me aware of it. I need to take care of that; that's more or less what I was getting at.  In these times, it will be something I have to deal with.  That's probably what you were getting at Something I have to deal with all season I understand it, one way or another. Yes, when you have such a serious injury and come back, you have to – and you didn't have to do this before – do rehab again and again, for weeks on end, to stay strong, keep up with the latest developments and get stronger so that you can get back to where you were. Because it takes a while, regardless of whether you have surgery or not and simply tear something, or whether you simply overexert yourself. You know, if you can do the rehab measures, the massages and the treatments to make sure you 're ready to go, then you're not overworked or anything, but can just focus on it over the weeks. So you don't feel like you're playing with an injury, right? No, not at the moment.  Did you go into the week without games in a variety of different situations ?  You went into this week after one of your worst games .  Didn't you remember that at all?  Do you even remember that? Or how did it affect your self-assessment for the second half of the season ? Yes, two of them were strange. One was a bad decision, and in the other, the ball bounced in the air So, you know, the ball simply didn't touch the ground in these situations , which has happened in the past and will happen in the past. But, um, you know, it's frustrating, of course.  You don't want to just go out and block four passes.  That 's never what anyone wants to do.  That's never the plan, of course. And the biggest part of the frustration is the feeling that I never want to let my teammates down .  That's always a big problem for me.  And in such situations, I feel that I have done that .  And that's the frustrating part that lingers.  And um, you know, I think that's what lingers.  But the other half is that I've already had to block three passes in important games.  I've made picks before, picks that decided the game and so on.  So, I'm leaving that behind me.  I've put that behind me. It's more about how I can improve.  What can I do better I'll just find a way to become more consistent .  And in other situations, where I don't make a stupid decision like in the first one, I try to either get the ball out of play or something like that. I just get it out of play Yes, with this game, with the way the Bucs blitzed, you obviously won't be playing against them again in the regular season, but it 's a league of imitators.  The teams might see that and think, and you were also successful against lightning this year .  How do you deal with that? You think to yourselves: Hey, this team could do it.  What can I do to ensure we are prepared? Yes, I think, as you said, it 's a copycat league.  It will be visible here soon. Who knows, maybe this week, next week, the week after, or in the off-season, whenever that may be .   In my opinion, it will happen eventually. But we need to think about it again and will take a look at it. As I said, we've reconsidered and already looked into it We fixed it, we fixed it.  And as far as I'm concerned in this situation, if it happens, I mean, there are times when people get through, and that's happened to me throughout my entire career .  It will happen to me for the rest of my career. It's simply that the ball goes out of bounds or something like that. Um, and the others just don't make bad decisions. I know you're focused on the Saints this week, but when you look at the NFC North and how competitive it is, and know what's coming next, how do you manage to stay grounded in the moment while knowing you have so much to do to get the game right? Yes, I think that's the point, that we have to do our part.  And our part is to play one-nil every week.  Um, I think that's what it boils down to .  You're not focusing on the next eight games from now on, because we haven't played those eight games yet.  Um, you're not focused on next week or the week after, and who's coming, and when the best or worst times are, when we're going to play all that, you know, you're focused on us playing at 12 this week.  Um, so you concentrate on being prepared for that moment when the ball is snapped for the first time , the whistle blows, and you concentrate on being 1-0 up this week.  And when next week rolls around, we'll focus on being 1-0 up this week .  And if you keep the score 1:0 every week and focus on that every week, you will eventually be where you want to be. And to get back to Caitlyn's question : What do you think about the pressure that's on the line every week, is so high in the NFC and in the division, but also in the conference as a whole? I mean, it's possible to have two seeded players eliminated from the playoffs within a week or two, not you specifically, but that can happen to anyone considering how many good teams there are. Yes, um, we don't have that kind of pressure here in the building.  I think the most important thing for us to understand is that only what we think, what we feel, counts. In one week we could be Super Bowl contenders, in one week playoff contenders, and in one week wild card contenders.  In a week we could be the worst team in the league. That's due to the noise from outside and all that.  But deep down, we think we know who we are. We are confident in who we are, what we are building, and what we are striving for. And as I said, we simply need to concentrate on keeping a 1-0 scoreline every week Then all the pressure disappears. What would it mean to have Kyle back in the backfield? Yes, that would be great.  They want their playmakers out there.  And he's one of those types for us.  We boys have obviously improved. Swift, you know, did a great job .  Other guys stepped in , you know, as replacements, Roshan and all the others.  So, as I said, it would be great to see him again.  Uh, we look forward to seeing him again, whenever that may be .  I don't know the exact timeline for all of this, but I know he was out there with us today.  He looked good.  He moved well and ran fast. Uh, and I look forward to seeing him whenever he's out there for us on Sundays Dan said that Luther was cleared from the concussion protocol. How big a role did he play in the offense and what kind of relationship have you built with him?   Yes .  Yes.  Uh, Luther is very important for this offensive.  I mean, he did, I mean, he did, how was it again? 40, 50, 60 yard pass to the crib on a 5 yard route. This is Luther. I talk about him every week when we're up here or whenever I have the opportunity, simply because he's special to us. He is explosive.  He makes moves.  He will continue to make moves.  He will always get up and celebrate, giving us energy and vitality as a team and as an offense And the fact that he has now been acquitted is exciting. I checked on him a few times during the short break we had. And he said he felt good.  I'm so happy to see him out there again.  A few more. Melissa. Caleb, I'm writing about how Chicago is now Caleb's city, with you and Caleb Wilson.   Yes Um, I was wondering, firstly, do you know why your parents named you Caleb And secondly, uh, would you like to play a role in Caleb Wilson's life, as he faces the same challenges as you?   Yes .  Um, the first part, yes.  Um, that's in the Bible. Um, and that's where it comes from.  That's the simple, simple answer to that. Um, Caleb is in the Bible, that's where it comes from. And then, um, the second point is, if he needs help, if he needs recommendations for anything, if he needs anything at all, uh, we build this friendship, this bond, this trust between us. Um, you know, that will happen naturally over time.   Um , but like I said, if he needs anything, I'm always happy to help him .  As you said, we're going through a very similar situation right now; he's joining a team that's not doing so well at the moment.  Um, and that was in my first year.  We didn't win as many games as we wanted, that's to be expected in my first year Um, and I heard him say that he'd never been in a situation like that before, and the coaches and so on. And so if he needs anything, I'm always there, like I said. Dion Jade. Um, your intention to go to the Simeon Career Academy last week.   Yes What did that mean to you?  It meant a great deal to the children, of course. That was a very special moment. Why was that important to you? Yes, whenever I can donate my time, that is the most important thing in my opinion.  You can give gifts, do all those things, and you know, your parents or friends will come and, um, all that. But, um, if I have a little bit of free time , I can give something back, and I think the best thing about giving back is the time and the presence. And that's why I always stayed until it was over, until all the questions had been answered and asked. And I was able to just show up, and I think, as I said, that's the most important thing I've realized during my time in the community: It's important to be there, to be present, and to enjoy the moment. I think it also helps me whether it's after a good game or a bad game .  You also go to the hospital, to a children's hospital, during breaks, and get to know a different life.  You get swept along, and I get swept along like everyone else , in something like football.  I 'm at this great facility.  I can do all these great things.  I can go home and you know all of this. It grounds me. It's great to be able to bring them light that they might need or want. And as I said, it's great to be able to give something back, to be able to dedicate my time, energy and effort to it .  And as I said, it's great for me to see the smiles on their faces. Because you never realize how much influence you can have until you're there yourself. And I will do that as often as possible throughout my career. Can you take a look? Yes, I know, they lost two games , I think, by more than two points. Everything else was 1.2;  It was a really close call. Their record might not show what kind of team they are, but when we go out there , we have to give it our all and make it happen. The coach will give us a good plan , and as I said, we need to go out there with the right attitude and implement it.   Take a break, you need to spend some time celebrating with your friend.  Yes, with Pete.   Yes What was it like to celebrate this moment, film the video, and watch him enjoy what he deserved? Yes, that's also one of the coolest things about being here in Chicago and what we're building here. Um, it's not just the Chicago Bears , but us as athletes from Chicago. We have already discussed several times what we want to do for the city And that's just a small step for Pete himself and his career, but also for us as a circle of friends.  We want to support each other and be there for each other. They asked me if I wanted to participate in the video .  I said, "Of course . We want to celebrate him." I think it's really cool when I can sit back and watch him. We talked and asked each other questions. We are trying to figure out how we can improve for the organization, both as players and as friends, to do something for the city. Like I said, it was really cool to be able to celebrate him , meet his friends and family, and hang out with him And to celebrate him at the end of the evening. He told me that he cannot imagine taking on responsibility because he knows what it means to be an athlete.   Yes What do you take away from watching him ?  Do you see how he plays a little differently What do you learn when you watch him play baseball?   Yes Pete always has this energy.  He's such a nice guy, but when he's on the field, he turns into a little rocket. It's his energy, his running, and what he does for his team and the organization without it becoming physical.  It's his energy. He always has good energy.  If you've ever met him and spent time with him , which you probably all have, then you know that he always has a good energy around him And that's why I say that what's special about him and what he has done for himself, his organization, and his people. Is Tom big enough for two MVPs? Absolutely right. The Bears.

title: Carson Schwesinger Press Conference | November 18th, 2026
text: How do you how do you feel about this game being flex this Sunday night? >> Oh, I'm excited. It'll be it'll be fun to play. Uh obviously doesn't change anything throughout the week and everything, but um definitely fun to play at night. Takes you takes you back a little bit to high school, you know, when you're when you're playing, uh at night, uh under the lights. >> Do you think it's a sign of respect? >> Yeah, I mean, obviously, I don't know what goes into it. I don't pay attention uh too much to to why they did it or anything, but I'm excited for it. Is it cool for you to get your first chances from the United? >> Yeah. No, I'm very excited. Especially having it at home, I think is probably my favorite part. I think the the home crowd um as we've seen through all the home games has been electric and um you know, I love going out there and playing at home in front of the fans. >> What's most important for you this year? >> Yeah, I think uh the by-week obviously came at a good time. I think uh doing as much as I can to recover is is is definitely important and then um also just just looking back doing looking back through through the games and then also preparing for uh for next week. >> How much have you seen Rudy grow as a coordinator since you first met him back in April? >> I think a lot. I think um just just like all of us since April, we've we've all taken strides and and made steps. You you try things, things don't work. you you uh you figure out, you know, what what you want to do and things like that. And um I think uh we've been able as a defense to to all collectively do that together, which has been pretty cool. >> Are you surprised UCLA is undefeated? >> Um I don't want to say surprised. I'm I'm excited to to see what they've been doing this year. It's pretty cool. Uh I think the what what they have going there is pretty awesome and and hopefully they go out there finish out the year. I I believe that they will and and finish undefeated. We've asked you guys so much about the rush defense and I know last week you said we had some injury issues too. What's that process like for you guys this week to kind of look at it since it's been something that's really throughout the season? >> Yeah, I we'll go back and look at it and and obviously as as the season progress you see different different things that show up and so you fix something else and something new comes up, right? and and so it's a matter of trying to trying to figure out the the best ways to combat all that and um you know I think that that uh each week we're getting better and and figuring it out and then and then a lot of it comes down to just execution as well if we're able to execute what we're supposed to do um you know we'll hold people to to limited yards. How much is this week just I mean that ankle you know just I know it's probably not completely healed but you know it's always going to be kind of linger just because of nature but how big is this just for you to get a little bit healthy? >> Yeah, I think that's an emphasis obviously um you have to use this this this week uh to to get that recovery in and and figure out the best ways to do so. And so that's the plan and and uh you know I expect to come into uh How are you? >> Sunday night feeling very fresh. >> Awesome. >> Thanks, guys.

title: Denzel Ward Press Conference | November 18th, 2026
text: But how do you feel about being flex this Sunday night? >> Um, >> mixed emotions. I mean, I I like it because I I like the one o'clock games. I do like I do like the one:00 games. You know, you you play the game, had the rest of the day to chill, do what you want, but I do like the the atmosphere and everything of a night game and everything that comes with that. So, so it's cool. Wherever whatever time they want us to play, I'm uh I'm all for it. >> Is it a sign that people are taking notice of the season? >> Oh, yeah. That's definitely definitely a sign. But like I said, it's always the main focus always is winning. So, I mean, it don't matter if we don't go out there and do what we supposed to do. So, uh that's the main job is to go out there and win. >> How much I know we talked about it after the game, but just how much fun has this been? Right. You talked about winning, winning, winning. Yeah. Obviously, the last two years we didn't win a bunch. So, what's this season been like for you? >> Yeah, it's been fun, man. I've been enjoying it. Like you said, winning is fun and uh just going out there making plays and and this team, like I said, I think we got a really close group and uh just to be able to go out there and do it with those guys and have fun and run around is uh it's been great so far. >> You know, uh you talk a lot about young players having to learn on the, you know, learn on the job and everything, but you have a first time coordinator. How have you seen Rudy sort of learn and grow as this season has been going on? >> Yeah, I think he's learned pretty quickly. I mean, like early on in the year, I think we're just kind of finding ourselves, you know, not really knowing what calls uh works best for us. And, you know, I think we did a good job of kind of switching up the calls and uh just pretty much playing what works best for us, like putting us in great positions and um that's really where I've seen them grow this year. >> So many times over the last couple years, we about getting a ton of targets and teams trying to avoid you. So, I mean, when you have a game like the other day when you pass defense, were you like kind of shocked almost at this stage? >> Yeah, I was a little shocked at first. Um, they they got a couple little slants, a little quick little stuff. I'm like, yeah, I got to make them pay soon. They they throwing at me a little bit too much, but I I I enjoy it. I love when they throw at me. Like I said, I always welcome all the throws. So, you know, if you guys want to go tell every team we play the throw it throw it 21, I'll be ready, you know. But, uh, I just enjoyed the competition. Enjoyed, uh, helping a team. uh put us in great position to win the game and uh you know I just look forward to moments like that. >> Ask Todd why he thinks you've been playing as well as you have this year. Not that you haven't always, but and he pointed out he thinks the film study that you do and your ability to anticipate what the other team's going to do. >> How much do you get that to factor in three pass breakups and being around the ball? >> Yeah. Yeah. Yeah, I feel I just got a great recognition of the game and um I'm able to kind of see plays before they come and um yeah, just let my talents and abilities take over and and that's it. You know, I have fun doing this and um that's it. It's just having fun. I just be having fun out there just looking to go make plays, get interceptions, and and everything else, you know, I just see how it falls at the end of the day. I guess off of that, what's maybe I feel like every year we're kind of asking you if you think you're you're playing the best you have in your career, >> whereas like you're topping even your previous years this year. >> What's the key to for you to not get complacent or as as a player in this league, not just feel like, hey, I've reached my peak, like I'm good, I got another payday, and just kind of keep working better. >> Oh, I think the biggest thing for me is that I don't play for money and I don't play for I don't know, I don't I don't play for accolades and and and recognition and stuff like that. Like I truly feel like I play the game just cuz I love it. Like I love playing football. Uh this is a dream that, you know, always had since a little kid to play in the NFL and and play football. So just to be able to live that dream out and play the game, that's that's really what motivates me to uh keep going and and like I want to be the best. I feel I am the best, but there's always way uh ways to get better and uh ways to grow and uh that's just what I love to do every day. But I'm just playing a kids game and that's that's what motivate me. How have you seen Miles Harden kind of grow into that? >> Yeah, man. Miles, he's he's came on huge, man. He's been he's been good foundation piece for us at that nickel position. Uh just making plays all over the field, getting sacks, covering well, and um I mean, can't say enough good things about him, just what he's been able to do for us, uh especially in crucial moments of the game and making plays. But, uh a great communicator out there, got us getting us on the same page and getting us in the right calls and uh he's been great for us. What can you say about Emanuel that you know had to get thrust into a sort of a starting role earlier in the season when Grant got one game and then steps into another starting role last week and plays as well as he did to be a rookie. How come he's picking things up? Just just say about him and his work ethic and what >> Definitely, man. Eman's a baller. Like I said, he's always in his playbook. Always he he knows what he's doing out there. Like I said, he's he's a rookie, but he's not playing like it at all. You know, I I was sad for him that uh that interception got taken away from him. That was a crazy play, but uh that just shows who he is, man. He's going out there making plays as a rookie all over the field. And uh like I said, he's a starter for us. He's going to be out there. We need him out there more and uh he's just been making plays all day. >> How important is it to you as a Cleveland native and someone who was born and raised here for you guys to be going home to this big game and really lighting it up down there. >> Yeah. >> Yeah. It's huge. It's fun. It's a It's an exciting atmosphere to be in Cleveland right now. Like I said, we looking forward to getting back and getting in front of those fans. Uh come come to the night game and uh it's going to be exciting. We just got to keep winning and uh take it one game at a time and and hopefully get to our goals at the end of the season. >> What do you think the biggest impact that Todd had that Todd has had? I mean, I know he's a head coach. hands everything. But the biggest change is >> um I think the biggest thing is just uh he doesn't let us settle like for nothing less than being great. Uh just out there on the practice field like I said he we be out there practice all day. So and that's pretty much just cuz we go we go get it right. We going to get the football right and uh we going to be out there until we don't get it wrong. So, I think that's the biggest thing, just making sure everybody's on the same page, knowing what they're doing uh come game time and um like I said, he's passionate about the game and he's just somebody that's easy to get behind and uh play for in the playoffs. >> What do you remember about playing you have a message for for your >> Yeah, it was it was fun, man. Exciting time. I remember uh going to the state championship game uh back when I was in high school in Erdonia. So, definitely wishing those guys the best of luck, man. Uh hopefully they go win it all. I'm going to be watching for sure. >> Thank you guys.

title: Todd Monken Press Conference | November 18th, 2026
text: First of all, Todd, how do you guys feel? How do you feel about being flex to Sunday night football and kind of how exciting is that for you guys? >> Well, I think it's really cool, you know, for our players. Um, I said it at the beginning of the year. I mean, you want to be on Thursday night, Sunday night, Monday night, you want to be flexed. Means you're having a good year. Uh, as nice it as it is to have a one:00 schedule every week. I mean, I said that, you know, early in the week. I mean, it's you're on a trajectory to be fired at some point because you're at one o'clock every week. So, you're fighting like hell to get to where, you know, you're on national TV. So, if people are going to watch football and more importantly than that, an opportunity to get to seven. You >> think that would be a good screen test for your young team with bigger games to follow? Oh, I think so. I think um you earn where you're at at the present moment and that only lends itself to what's in front of you and how important that's going to become. Uh you know, getting the buy at six and four and putting yourself in position where the rest of the games matter and especially uh the one coming up. Judging from that first um Thursday night game that you guys had against the Steelers, uh you know, how how rocking was that uh for all you guys and is that what you're expecting for the Sunday game? >> Oh, it was a huge advantage. Huge advantage. Um making hard for the opposing offense cadence wise, being able to function and making an advantage for us when we're on offense. I mean, it's a huge advantage and it should be playing at home. >> Are you looking forward to a check with Mike? >> I am. I'm a big Mike Tyland fan. I mean, people have made more out of this uh than it really is. Um because I am a believer in um you are who how you play as a player, as an organization, as a coach. That that that's you on the field. That's your team. That's your name. That's what started all that at Tampa. It all started I was talking about the name on your jersey be it the Browns or your individual name is you you want to change a narrative play better individually and collectively and that the only way you can do that is through hard work and a day-to-day approach and uh that that's really all it is that that you know that I was getting at and um our guys have done that. Todd, how much do you balance kind of internal, you know, scouting, you know, looking at yourselves with looking ahead to the next opponent when you're in this during the bye? >> Both. I think you do internal scouting. You look at other situational football from around the league. What are we doing? What aren't we doing? What are other people doing? And then you're taking a look at the Raiders. All the above. when you're trying to get a little bit ahead. Like I told the staff, it'd be a damn shame if we don't take at least some amount of time and get ourselves ahead on the Raiders so we're not scrambling. There's no reason next week with Thanksgiving to be scrambling. There's no reason to not, you know, be in position where we're ahead and really start to narrow uh how we want to attack them and how we want to defend them. And that's that's uh obviously what we're going to do. I know you always believed from the start of the season that this is what you were capable of. You've even said you haven't even scratched the surface about like your potential, but six and four is a a pleasant surprise to a lot of fans and obviously nationally you guys are becoming a positive story. Is there something about the first half of this season that's been a pleasant surprise for you as as the coach? >> I wouldn't say that. Uh like like I've said plenty of times, um the biggest surprise was how we played at Jacksonville. That that was the biggest surprise. Um with our off season and training camp, uh I did not anticipate that. I did anticipate the way we've played since then. And even though we weren't clean, we earned uh that lopsided loss at Pittsburgh. Our guys fought and they battled. We just we didn't coach well enough. We didn't play well enough. But from the day I got here, I appreciate the way our guys worked and competed, wanted to be coached, allowed themselves to be coached. And uh so there's nothing really surprising when you have a group of coaches and players that we have that continue to battle and fight and have perseverance and work every day to get better. Um, and that's what they've done. And it's not not been perfect. I mean, for sure. But our guys have battled the finish and it's a real credit to them. >> What kind of boost has uh Dylan Samson been able to give you and the ability for him to catch like the wheel route, but also run between the tackles? >> Well, he's he's got versatility, which is critical, you know, not only his ability to run the football, but in the pass game. I think that's where it where it shows up and the protections, you know, he's our third down back. So, we lost that. Now, we lost Rocket, you know, and and not that J-Mack and Audrey and those guys stepped in and uh but but ultimately um those guys were a big part of what we do and Dylan is that and it's been nice to have him healthy because he's wired the right way. Comes to practice every day. He's diligent and he's only going to continue to get better. Tom, how would you just assess and and you know for rookies, especially Casey and Denzel and how they've come in in this offense and you know where they're at at this sort of midway point? >> Well, it's it's a credit to them. They're they're wired the right way. I mean, it's Andrew and his staff doing a great job behind the scenes to drill down, you know, what makes individual players tick and do they fit who we want to bring in the building terms of their diligence, their work ethic, their grit, their mental stamina, and they have that. And so that's what makes them who they are. I think it's it's it's easier to see a player's skill set. You know, you can turn on the tape and say, you know, balance, body control, quickness, acceleration, catch radius, but drilling down to what's going to separate them from the pack of others um is a real credit to Andrew and his staff and and how those guys are wired. Talked a lot about first year players having to learn as they go and you know as as but you have three firsttime coordinators. What's that growth process like and how much is there a learning curve there for and how much have you seen those three guys sort of grow over the course of this season? >> Well, that's all of us, right? First time doing it together. And a lot of that came from early on from a visit with Mike McDonald about it and him choosing his staff and he talked about, you know, you've got to fight uh to get the coaches you want and you might have to get them a year early. You might have to for rising superstars because if you wait, you won't get them. And that's what I saw in the guys that we have. I saw Travis Schwitzer when we were together in Baltimore. I saw that in Rudy and I saw it in Byron. And they're wired the right way and and how I see things. And that's the most important thing is self-awareness, um a diligence, a work ethic, a loyalty, um that they understand that we're human and we're going to fail, but we're gonna fight like hell to fix it. We're always under construction. You guys will keep hearing me say that, but that is true. And that's what I love about our guys is that uh as coaches, coordinators, and our staff is that it's a we thing. We continue to fight and scratch and get better and try to chase edges, you know, in terms of getting better and uh we haven't been perfect. There's been a lot of things that that we can certainly do better. Uh but uh but I'm awfully proud of those guys and we're going to continue to to fight together and get better. text: It's the It's the busting the door open. >> Bust it open. Got a lot of energy this morning. Got a lot a lot of energy this morning. Jordan is um having surgery today. biggers will go on IR. Um so he'll be done for the year and um you know we'll miss those guys. It's Jordan Phillips and Zeke. Jordan was having a great year. I mean really I mean just watching the way he played, the toughness, what he was able to do for our defense, the plays he was making. And I'll tell you this too, Zeke, I mean Zeke took a huge step, huge step. and um not only playing inside but playing big end position, the versatility that he had. I mean, those are two players who will be really missed. Obviously, you know, top that on with Zach not being here, but those guys um what they've showed us in this year, they got a very, very bright future. So, I know this is hard for them right now and hard for our team, but um those guys those guys are good football players and they're going to have really good careers in the NFL. So, wishing them the best and um they'll be missed. Jordan out for the year as well. >> And how does a head coach react when it was your three highest use of defensive tackles for the season within a span of eight days? Were you shell shocked? What what kind of emotion? >> Um, it's hard, but then, you know, I think often times the way you have to approach things, there's there's something that happens and you got to react to it and you got to move on. And it doesn't mean that you don't care. It doesn't mean that you don't miss them. It doesn't mean that you're not sad and disappointed. But you have to move on and you can't look back and you just have to move forward in this league. So then it it's what's our response going to be and it's who who do we have who do we have left? Who can we pull up from the practice squad? Is there anybody out there that can help us? And and you have to move forward. So is it hard losing three guys to IR all at the same position with the span of a couple days? Yeah. I mean for sure it's um but now there's a challenge in front of us and just there's been a lot of challenges. So, let's see how we react and how we respond and move forward. >> Can you characterize what it'll take to do exactly that? Not not to ask too broad of a question, but uh from if it's KG, uh Jordan Jefferson coming up now. >> I mean, it's it's going to be KG's KG's turn, he's going to play more, right? He he's going to have to I mean, we finished that game with KG and Cooper who got here three or four days before that game and and and he played a lot and he did a nice job. I mean, give him a lot of credit. He was on a practice squad in Carolina. He comes here and all of a sudden now he's a starter, you know. So that's the NFL. That's opportunity, you know. So let's coach him. Austin's going to coach him. Austin's going to coach him up. He's going to meet with him extra. And um he's got an opportunity in this league now to be a starting defensive tackle. So he'll embrace it. We'll embrace it. And then, you know, you look at that's a position where you have to heavily rotate because those guys can't play 40, 50 snaps a game. Usually you go four or five deep. So, who are the next guys up? And that's what we need to find this week in practice. Who are the next guys like a Jefferson, right? Those are the guys that we're going to have to see. And and we're gonna have to get them ready to go because this is this is a a great football team that we're about to play. So, we we'll embrace the opportunity. >> How would you describe the message that you have or will deliver to the team relative to the biggest moment of adversity so far this season? >> Yeah, just like everything else that we do, stay focused on today. What can you do better today to help this football team? I mean, and what can we do better, right? Like even for a guy like Jordan Brooks who right now, I think is playing out of his mind. I mean, I think he is. I know he is. He's playing at an allp pro level. He he is and he's showing that and he's getting better as the season goes. And I think he's playing some of his best football. So, even for him, what can he do better today so he can play even better on Sunday? So, how can we all get together and pick it up just a little bit to fill in for that void? I mean, what else can we do? this year, guys. This year is full of adversity. I mean, we lose our quarterback. We lose one of the best running backs in the league. We got all these rookies. It's just so what? Like, what are we going to do about it? We all have to be at our best. We can't sulk. We have to understand the situation and we got to work. And um you know when Sunday comes the one thing I know about this team they are going to go out there and they are going to compete and they're going to play hard and they're going to stay together and we'll figure out the rest >> without divulging without divulging game plan and more generally speaking when you get a rash of injuries like that to one group. Is it how do you balance the impact of changing what you do because of the loss of players versus trying to find guys that can do what you were doing previously? >> It's it's hard. It's um you know just when you're starting to do more schematically because guys are getting comfortable with the foundation and we're building and you're starting to see these pressures and these movements and these different looks. We got to be careful now, right? Because the the quickest way to give up plays is to have guys really not comfortable or not know what they're doing. And that's not fair. So we need to figure out very fast in these next few practices, what can we do? What can we execute? What's fair of us to ask them to go out and execute with just a few practices? and we're gonna have to go out and play. Um, but that's going to be a challenge to us as coaches. Uh, it's going to be a challenge to the players so we can continue to move this forward, but then at the same time, we got to find extra meeting time, uh, extra walkthrough time. And I, like I said, I have a lot of confidence in Austin and the D staff that we'll continue to develop the new guys who come in. >> If I may continue on this line of questioning, um, Austin Clark was one of the few coaches that you retained here. >> What went into your decision to do that? Um, and I he's been retained just by just about everybody. But what what what was the mindset with that decision? >> Um, he's worked with a bunch of very close friends of mine that, you know, called me as soon as I got the job and and I've known about him. I knew his reputation. Um, some from people that I really trust. And when I got here, I sat down with him. I talked to him quite a bit. And, um, I just had a really good feeling about him. um the guys that he's coached, studying the film, the work that he's done, and um now that I've been with him, how how hard he coaches, how demanding he is, he gets the most out of his players, and it shows up on tape. They're getting better, right? How do you how do you judge that? Something you turn on the tape and you watch the progress a group has made and I see it on tape. But that's that's what led me to keep them. >> Is Brewer still in concussion protocol? >> Brewer is in the protocol. >> Practicing today practicing today. >> Brewer will not practice today. wanted to ask you about um the run game and the run defense, two areas that are crucial to this team and its identity. Um what have you seen from them? What do you expect to see from them? Understanding that Han has been out now you've lost these three defensive tackles. Um you're seeing the eightman fronts that have limited you guys to 74, 77, 78 yards. Run defense, you've allowed six consecutive opponents to rush for 100. And I know you're a young team and you've got injuries, but tell me about what you've seen from those two areas because it I know you play hard in both areas. >> Yeah. Answer first on defense. The run defense has improved every week. I mean, you can look at 150 yards, 170 yards. Well, did they run the ball 40 times and how many points did they score? Right? I mean, the last two opponents that we played against had really good running attacks. And when you look at the stat sheet, the rushing yards might have been high, but the yards per carry weren't. And we gave up on defense, we gave up two touchdowns against the um Colts, right? The defense gave up a touchdown. That's 17 points. And against the Lions, the defense gave up one touchdown, you know? So, so what we're doing in the run game right now, I think we're doing a pretty good job there. Certain certainly there was some on the perimeter that got away from us last week that that we need to fix. Um, is there going to be a challenge going forward now with with some, you know, some new guys and potentially some new things we need to do? Sure. Um, but I'm I'm confident in the run defense. Um, as far as the offense goes, it's it's kind of like I said to you, when you load up the box and you're sending guys off the edge and you're pressuring, what happens is you see the checkown start to open up last week, the catch and run by Ali down the sideline, the catch and run by Herm for the first down. I mean, those are the things. Now, there's going to be things that start to open up that we have to take advantage of. And then the more that we do that, the more the run game will start to open up again because we'll force defenses to have to go back instead of continue to come forward. So, it all ties in together. The pass game's tied to the run game. You know, >> the Buffalo Bills have been such a mental hurdle for previous iterations of this team, this franchise in in recent memory. Um, you haven't been here for that. A lot of these players haven't been here for that. So, are you guys almost exempt from that mindset and kind of like fresh slate? Uh, you don't know anything about this recent history with >> the first time that I've coached against them. I have obviously a lot of respect for what they've done this year. Obviously, I respect what they've been able to do historically, but but what they've done in the past and what we've done in the past have really no meaning to what's ahead in the future. Um, you know, look, you you watch them and you look at their players in really offense and defense and special teams and they are clearly one of the most talented teams in the NFL. Um, it's the first time I've really got a chance to study them because I was in the NFC and we never had crossover and I've obviously appreciate and respected their players by watching on TV, but I've never studied the quarterback. I mean, he's about as good as it gets. And you know, the offensive line probably doesn't deserve doesn't get enough credit. Um, but the way they play together as a whole, they're really well coached and I think they're one of the best units that plays together. The back is explosive. I mean, very similar to playing Gibbs in Detroit. He's able to do all those things as a runner. The way he cuts the ball back, the way he catches the ball out of the back field, they got dynamic receivers. They got tight ends who play like receivers. Um, and then defense, what jumps out to me is the Dline and and all the the players that they have up front. I think Jimmy Leonard does a really good job. I know Jimmy well. I coached him in Cleveland. Um, and he's sound and they're very talented and they've gotten better each week. And, you know, saying all of that with their players. Um, I also, this isn't a team that just has good players and they're good behav because they have good players. They're they're well coached. Joe does a good job. I've known Joe for a while. um he does a great job with the offense and I mean they're a great team. I mean I have a ton of respect for very similar for the other really good teams that we've played this year. So we'll we'll do everything we can this week and we'll uh we'll get out there on Sunday and we'll give them everything that we got just like we have every single week. >> Olson has made some long kicks in his career 60 58 57 56 but in the last three years 50 plus only 58% so less consistency in the last three years. I'm curious, this team, this moment in time, this season, are you leaning a little toward more towards the importance of accuracy from 50 under as opposed to leg strength 50 to 60? >> Um, consistency is what I'm looking for. If I had to give you anything, just want to see consistency and once we know the range that that we'll see the consistency, then it will allow us to call the game and make key decisions in the game better, you know, and that's I think that's the key for me right now. >> I wanted to ask about the end of the Colts game. Fourth and 17, three timeouts. Um you're kind of in that gray area though um field position wise. Why did you decide to go for it versus a punt? >> Yeah, based on here, we would have had very little. we would have had to use our timeouts right with little time left and with the way they were running the ball at that point of the game and our situation. I just felt like it gave us the best shot right there with the little time if we stopped them and the little time that we would have had if we would be able to stop him. We just felt it was in our best decision. But we did talk about it. We just felt in that moment it was the best decision for us. How much do you think obviously playing in the NFL is is is new for everybody, but with Kyle and Cord um new experiences, new teams are going to obviously adjust to how they play him. Um how much do you think you can expect to see growth this week >> from Kyle? I think he'll I think he'll take a good step. Um you know, just think about the first time going out there early on, the anxiety, the speed of the game, um the unknown. you know what what and even in the conversations with him how were they going to play him you know and it took him a little time to get that you saw him the ball start to come out quicker he saw it a little better just to get into a rhythm get into a routine you know it's um hasn't had that many reps so he gets all the reps again this week with the offense going over similar plays and getting better and then just not his first time going through the pregame as the starter all that stuff I'd expect him to be much calmer and he was pretty calm but just internally I think it will be easier for him it'll slow down for And you know, I'd expect him to play better. >> Is a plan with Chris Bell to rest him this week or just expect him back to practice? >> No, Chris, I would say Chris will be dayto day. I mean, so we'll see if we we'll see if we get him for this week. >> It's kind of a mid-season point. A lot of us do our, you know, mid-season reviews. I wanted to ask you about Malik Washington, who seems like he could be a MVP candidate on this team. He runs the ball. He catches the ball. Throws a touchdown pass, punt return, kick return, even has a tackle. What's been his value and and what does he do for this team? And and maybe pound for pound the toughest player on this team. >> Yeah, Malik's done a great job. Um I thought he played really well against the Colts. Obviously, the pass jumps out, but but he had some really good catches and even there was another rep I showed the the team today. He on one of the third downs, he had such a good release on the corner. He spun the corner around. he ran his route and he had him beat so bad where he got a penalty on the play. So, those don't show up on the stat sheet, but that's just as good as another 15 yard catch. Um, I would say consistency, his leadership has picked up. Uh, he's done a good job with Kyle. Um, Kyle trusts him and I think he's earned the trust not only of, you know, both quarterbacks and the offense, but the staff. And, um, you know, while his production might not be where he wants it to be or as good as it could be, he's really having a nice year. 61 in Orchard Park on Sunday. We like that. >> We like that for a uh mid November. >> Do you? >> I don't care what the temperature is. >> Really? You know, you me doesn't bother you. >> No. No. It was 60 something degrees this morning when I got up. >> He's going to take out his double radar shortly. >> Just a random a rand really random question. Why four receivers on the practice squad at the moment? Are you dealing with anything else on a 53 at receiver besides Chris Bill? >> Just practice and just guys to take a look at. So, um, you know, just kind of trying to turn through and find some more guys there. >> With the, uh, obviously you got the issues at defensive tackle, the new faces, but how much can Malik Herring or um, >> what? No, the the actually the the big ends, how much can they help you in terms of the inside? Yeah. >> Um, you know, possibly a little bit. It's still, you know, it's for some guys can, you know, so we'll see. We're going to we're going to work a bunch of guys around to see what they can do. Usually it's the bigger tackles can go outside. Not many of the bigger ends go inside. Um, but we've used Malik in a lot of different spots, so we'll see what he can do. You know, Sean and Austin have been talking a lot about the different ways to get different guys in certain situations, and they'll continue to do so, and they've done a great job. >> Good. >> Thank you. >> All right, guys.

title: Patriots' identity crisis is a Mike Vrabel problem
text: All right, a day later than normal, but I like to think at least $1 better here in the Patriots Interference podcast. It is Tuesday morning on the banged up, bummed out CLNS Media Network. I'm back from Munich with a crippling addiction to the Haribo gummy bears uh takes than I think I have had and thoughts maybe for any episode you and I have done typically Monday nights with Mike Girardi. A love of Aaron Rodgers, shout out to the best plane Wi-Fi I've ever had. And a welcome home dirty diaper from my daughter that I I wanted to call the cops on my 1-year-old [laughter] because this was just absolutely something this morning. Anyway, by the time folks listen to this cuz you and I are are recording now Tuesday morning, it will be Tuesday night or Wednesday and two things will have happened. Number one, we will have a definitive report. None of this believed to be expected, thinking, fearful of yada yada about Drake Maye's ankle, which might even be a lower leg for all we know. Right now, what we do know is that they are concerned he has sustained a fractured ankle, that he is expected to miss an extended period, which means probably this season. That is according to Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport, who can't agree where Drake Maye is at the moment, but both agree this is bad. Number two, what will happen by the time you listen to this, I will be either prepping or recording a solo podcast on Wednesday answering all the mailbag questions that folks uh who actually heard from on this trip from France and North Carolina and thank you to everyone who stopped by uh asked over the last I don't know 12 hours. So if you still have questions, get them in ASAP. I will get to every single one before I am off Thursday through Sunday, much like the Patriots, because this bye week, let me tell you, comes at a good time for everyone. Uh Mike Girardi, life has changed. I'm going to ask you something I never do because I think it's just terrible content and we [snorts] are here for the audience, not for ourselves. But how are you? >> Just just ducky, man. Had to had to power through the the NFL pros sideline view of the of the broadcast well the broadcast. We get the all 22s, right? You get the behind the the center which was fine, but the German all 22 from the sideline was an absolute debacle. Plays over here, cameras over there, cameras in the stands, cameras up in the ceiling. So yeah, good job by them. >> Okay. So just as I expected, you are upset like a lot of people listening to this, but not for the same reason. It's about the camera work which look, I had to work from the TV copy cuz you don't get the all 22 via NFL Plus over in Europe. I don't know why that is. I think if you pay for a service, they should not care where you are. They can report the NFL can wherever I am, get it wrong, get it right. Doesn't matter as long as they give me what I paid for. Didn't happen, so we have these workarounds with some you know copies of the broadcast that can be found elsewhere on the internet. But the point is I want to start with the obvious so that we can kind of clear this out of the way cuz we have a ton to get to. I am going to list a number of things here. If you have any quibbles or notice any omissions, please state so and then we'll get right into why this team is in a lot of trouble and that's even independent of their star quarterback, franchise quarterback being out for the rest of the year when they need to win some games now at five and five um with some tough games ahead. Okay. Number one, May's injury is obviously an earthquake. This is a tectonic shift for the season in terms of expectations, their ceiling, their hope, what the rest of the year means, coaches, players, everybody else moving forward. Some people have said the season was lost. I thought that was premature until we got May's injury reported. But look, if they make the playoffs right now, it is something close to a miracle based on what we saw from Tommy DeVito who I think will be better by the way and I do think will start. But nonetheless, you look at the schedule, how they played lately. This season was risking life support status where it is now based on the way their defense has been. But anyway, everything is changed. We all get that. Number two. May's ankle injury is the latest and worst blow to the most injured team in football. Even if they were overachieving and they maximized every player and talent and skill and scheme, the injury luck alone this year would have kept the Patriots from the Super Bowl period. This is a season from hell injury wise. Number three. This team is not overachieving. It is in fact regressing. They are two and three over the last five games. They have yet to beat a team with a good quarterback and a good proven head coach. The only argument you could have against that is Josh Allen and Joe Brady. And Joe Brady's team is eight and one. Good for Joe Brady. I think you could very clearly see in that Patriots game he was out coached. Let's set that to the side. They are one of the worst defenses in football lately. They're allowing explosive plays. They don't get turnovers. Their run game aside from playing the Dolphins and the Jets and the drags of the league doesn't move anybody. The offense was May. The defense is missing. This team is not overachieving. It's regressing. Number four. The roster is good, not great. The depth problems were real. The front office, I believe, and and this is a change of opinion for me, was right to hold on to some of their draft picks, especially in the offensive and defensive line. Those have been real problems. Number five. Mike Vrabel's messaging is not quite at the level of like when we all talked about Jerod Mayo's press conferences as much as we did Jerod Mayo's football team. But they've become headlines. How much you care about that is a case by case basis. It's up to you. You don't have to care about this at all. But it has become a topic nationally including on Football Night in America on Sunday Night on NBC. It's obviously on local radio, TV, podcast and will be here today. The last one, six, which I think goes without saying, but I I want to reiterate this anyway at the lowest point of the Patriots season. Jerod and I are not podcasting contrary to some of my mentions, out of joy that the season is now a pit of misery. Okay, we are here and have been through thick and thin. And we will be here through thick and thin if they make a run to the playoffs, celebrating the good football, which is what we'd like to see. We would all like to see this. Reporter, fan, analyst, coach, player, this is what you wait the rest of the year for is to see football and played well and hopefully competitively. That's lacking right now. Um maybe it'd be better if we had some more notebooks talking to each other, but right now we do not. The Patriots are a whole. We are always here to explain why and just as when they beat the Bills and blow out the Raiders, which is really after that game the season turned, we were telling you why they are still the team you thought they were, what's happened since has proven that wrong. And again, good or bad, we're here to explain it. Did I miss anything? Did I say anything wrong? Or can we dive deeper into what's going on here like we like we like to? >> Yeah. No, and I would just say on the on your on your last point just about uh the way we get perceived sometimes. I always say the job's the same, win or lose, but I will say from a selfish standpoint, give me good football over bad football any day of the week. We we live through some really tough seasons with Belichick and Mayo after 20 years of me covering the team and then being pretty much awesome every single year and pretty much punching a ticket to at least the AFC Championship game if not the Super Bowl every other year. So when they're bad, you feel it. It's everybody feels it. You people invest a lot of money and effort and time into the team and we obviously it's our living. Um and again, just the job's the same, but I would always take um better football over what we've seen the last couple weeks for sure. >> Yeah, and I I don't want to belabor this point much more because people are investing their time with us and that is something you will never get back in the way that none of us get our time back. So it's really deeply appreciated on our end. But I will say like the times that I've caught myself almost sounding angry uh on this show, it's it's it's not because they're winning. You know what I mean? Like and that doesn't mean I'm rooting for the outcome of the negotiation and the Christian Gonzalez stuff, which I think I got fair blowback for, but it's just to say that, you know, the job is the job. We're here for it, and good or bad, I think we all understand that competitive, competent football is what we're all seeking here. Whatever the result is, it is. Uh and right now the Patriots have had a a long line of bad results here, even if they're close wins lately that we're going to get into. Now, May is missing is going to be missing. Again, putting all that to the side. I asked this question around the locker room in Munich after the Patriots lost obviously 35 to 10 in the lines. What is missing right now? Because I just think and we will dive into the stats and the tape, you just watch this team and go something's not right. And it sounds like basic, nebulous, almost useless analysis, but the players and coaches themselves admit that. And I got different answers. I do think the most honest of them, the most revealing, was from Christian Elliss, who echoed what Elliot Wolf had told me literally the day before about guys are not trusting one another in terms of I know he'll do his job, so I don't have to worry about that. I will do my job. And they have reason not to trust that in certain instances, which we'll get to. But if we accept that you are what you repeatedly do as a person, as a football team, as a player, as a coach, that means right now that the Patriots, who have been so inconsistent, whether they're looking over the shoulder or not, do not have an identity. And that is my answer to my own question. Vrabel has talked about that word over and over. And by their own definition of an identity, right? title: Cam Ward on the Offense Playing Free, Facing the Cowboys & His return in Texas | Press Conference
text: I know Robert talked earlier in the week and talked earlier just about a philosophical change that has allowed you to do more. Uh how have you liked that? Maybe how'd that come about in your mind? >> I think just getting back to the basics of what we all do offensively at a high level. Uh I think it's uh you know a lot of more up pace to what I like. It's a lot of you know getting the ball out, putting the ball in play. then, you know, we actually call a lot of shots is just, you know, being able to get the look that we want versus, you know, having to scramble around or do something. But I think the way we're trend is is going upward. >> Are you maybe campaigned for that yourself and glad your voice was heard? >> Uh, I would say so. Yes. But, uh, it's what we all want though because we know what makes us go as a offense, man. It's going to continue to, you know, continue to do good things for us in the future. with them uh potentially changing defensive players this week. Does that affect how you guys prepare at all or do you still go by what you know Dallas's tendencies are defensively? >> A little bit of everything. Always go by, you know, what they showed on film. They can't get too far away from it. They're this deep into the season and you know, you got to look at the play caller's past, what he like to do um situationally, you know, out of, you know, whether it's sudden changes, anything. Just try to look at, you know, different situations, what he did, try to, you know, compare the two. Taran, he he touched on just your comfort level being from doing things that that you did in college as far as like the temple and everything. >> Do you go to like do you guys discuss that where you go back and you look at some of the stuff you did at Miami, Washington State, etc. or is that something that just kind of organically came about? >> I'll say both. Um, they interviewed me the whole time during the draft process. Daves and Shay, they seen a lot of stuff what I did at UIW. That was what I was in. At Washington State, we did that. And in Miami, they didn't do a lot of it. And he, Coach Dawson, allowed me to bring that over there and it helped us. And I think here is going to do the same thing. >> A lot of people saying, "Man, they should have done it sooner." Coach kind of saying you needed to do certain things to kind of get to that point. Does it make sense like the progression it took to get here? >> It does, but I mean, at the end of the day, we were just trying to win games. It was some games that we didn't really need it. there some games it could have helped us. So, you know, it really depends on how the game was going and I think at the end of the day, you know, we always had a great game plan. It just always came down to the play to the players executing it. >> How much of a settling force has Schlloman been? And does he call the protections or do you >> he you talking about the my points? He call he calls the my points. Uh he's a big help for me and I think me and him always on the same page, you know, whether he calls or not. I'm always communicating with the back to who we're going to. But, you know, he does a he does an unbelievable job and I think he's for sure one of the best and smartest centers out there. >> How much do you feel like the game has slowed down for you in terms of processing at the line and with postnap reads and and everything like that that goes along with developing as a quarterback? >> It slowed down a lot. I see the field, you know, extremely well. I can tell you what coverage they're going to before, you know, it even happens. It's just, you know, the amount of film that we all watch together. So, it's really more of, you know, continuously getting better as soon as the coverage happened, where the ball is supposed to go versus how you have to react if the ball doesn't go there, trying to, you know, get the best outcome of the play. And I think just the more reps I get is that the more reps that I do, certain plays versus different coverages is going to continue to help me. >> Was there a point where you got where the light kind of came on or has it just been a gradual process over the course of the year? >> It's been a process. It's been a everyday challenge. Uh, getting better. you know, the the new receivers that we're going to have coming in continues to get rest with those guys to make sure that we're on the same page and I think he's gonna continue to get better. >> How to get Cornell back and what's the dialogue been with him while he's kind of been recovering? >> He's been a high spirit. Continue to stay in the playbook cuz it's hard, you know, if you're not getting reps, you know, and walk through to, you know, mentally have have and know each and every play. He he's been very good. He was out there today, you know, to walk through just continuously going through his process and, you know, I'm ready to see him back on the field. Nice to see his eight year too back on the 53. >> Oh yeah, that's that's exciting. Uh he's someone who's who deserves it. He's someone who, you know, he's here early. He he's putting in some extra work and so we got to continuously try to get him up to speed on the playbook and, you know, when he's in the game, try to give him, you know, plays to make plays. >> What aspects um do you think of your play are a little more visible now since the the shift in philosophy for the offense a few games ago? >> I think everything. I think we're more explosive. I think the the RPO game is helping to run game, you know, a lot. And I think we're able to see, you know, everybody's, you know, side of game that, you know, we haven't be able to see for a long time just because of, you know, we're all be able to play more free. We're all able to do the things we're good at. Um, especially the receiving room, the guys in space, they can make people miss. And so, you know, I think, you know, us shifting a little bit is going to continue to help us. >> Uh, growing up in Texas, where'd you stand on the Cowboys? Um, wasn't a huge fan, but you know, I mean, it's the Cowboys. >> What What uh what cleat do you wear with this uniform combination this week? >> Either blue or red, whichever ones. I mean, it's going Is this our first time wearing these combos? >> Yeah, >> the all blue and Tennessee, not just new jerseys. >> With the new jerseys. >> New jerseys. >> New jerseys. Man, that's going to look good. I tell you that right now. Look good >> defensively. They they've had some struggles defensively. What what what do they still concern you concern you of? >> Uh the concern is up front. Um they they're very agile, those big guys up there. I I think 25 is a very good corner. 13 he he's very good. I think they they they have a very good defense. I think things haven't gone their way. They've been in bad situations in some key parts of the game, whether it's field position or anything. And I think for us, we have to continue to put the ball in the space. We have to continue to take what the defense gives and I think it's going to really come down to, you know, who's more physical and who wants it more at the end of the day. >> I know your home is closer to Houston, but you got you have a lot of family coming to the game. >> Yeah, I think I saw my both sides of my family. My dad's side, my cousin, a lot more of my mom's side going into the game and, you know, some of my friends from high school pulling up. >> Do you get to watch a lot of college ball at all though? >> I do, but I only watch Miami and UIW. those the those are the only teams who come on at times where I'm able to watch and so you know I like watching you know UIW they throw it every play still when I was there I love watching and actually the the backup there he's the quarterback he was my backup at Wazu Emma Brown he's the quarterback there so it's crazy how you know you get connections with everybody and now he's playing at the school you started from he's doing good and so then Miami I mean they got a chance to to get in the playoff and so you know we we worried about getting that ACC championship that's all you know I know coach Crystal ball worried about trying to get an ACC championship and win it. >> So, you haven't seen much of what Coach Morris is doing with Mr. Baker out there? >> Oh, I I see it, but I ain't got a chance to really watch it. Um, they I watched last game. Who did they play? It was last Sunday. I mean, last Saturday. Who did they play? I couldn't remember. They played Tech. Uh, end up being a shootout, but you know, they they doing some good things and it's a lot of stuff. They doing signals out there. I'm calling out the play cuz I still remember the signals from Morris. So, you know, the the whole offense is it it breeds good quarterbacks. allows them to see the field and I think Morris he he's going to have that place you know in the playoff real soon. >> Cam Coach Sol said in terms of these offensive shifts that no one was really ready for it week one feels like you guys are ready for it now. Do you agree that this is the time to do or do you felt like maybe it could have been done a little bit earlier? >> I mean always I think it could have been done faster but I think it was done at the right time. I think it was you know the the situations that you know brought us to these circumstances. Um, I think it was, you know, points in the game where we wish we could have shift faster, but there was also, you know, a couple games where we didn't need it. So, I think it was a little bit of everything. It was just a perfect timing for it to happen. And, you know, we've we've been preparing for this moment as a whole offensive staff. And so, you know, we just ready to continue to learn each and every week on the the plays that we repping, new plays that we install and just trying to execute them on Sundays. >> Last one. >> In what ways have you seen some of the younger playmakers on this team gain confidence over the last three weeks with that philosophical change, too? It's all the same. Football's the same no matter it's, you know, it's a little bit faster, but you know, college NFL is not much different. Still guys got to tackle. Still guys got to catch the football. And I think that's the thing that I'm trying to, you know, communicate to those guys that go out there and make a play. I'mma put in your vicinity. Um, if I don't try to build me out, but I'm going be as accurate as I can and then, you know, have fun because we get eight more opportunities, you know, that's guaranteed. And so we we don't know what the future holds. And every time every time you get a chance to get on that field, uh, you got to go you got to go earn some money.
